title: Z-TAC enables custom and combinatorial degradation of cell surface proteins - Nature Communications
byline: Zhou; Dingjingyu; Shue; Lawrence; Cheng; Aoxing; Gao; Sean; Metivier; Rebecca J; Abeja; Dinah M; Donovan; Katherine A; Fischer; Eric S; Flynn; Ryan A; Xin
html:
Abstract

Cell-surface degrader platforms typically require target-specific engineering and have therefore been applied to a relatively small set of protein targets. Here we report Z-TAC, a strategy that enables plug-and-play conversion of existing IgG antibodies into cell-surface protein degraders. Across multiple single-span and multi-span targets from distinct protein families, Z-TAC induces efficient and sustained degradation of both individual receptors and receptor combinations. For a multi-span membrane receptor lacking selective antagonists, Z-TAC mediates complete receptor degradation and functional inhibition, demonstrating the ability of this platform to overcome the limitations of conventional pharmacological approaches. This study introduces a generalizable and scalable strategy for functional perturbation of the cell-surface proteome.
